ambient_trade.text: Salt out of Ighrast is fetching {gold} a sack in {town} this week, so I am buying wool at a fair price.
Wool wanted in {town}, paying well for clean bales. Bring them to my wagon before the tolls eat the profit.
Who has spare mules for the {town} road? I will pay {gold} and not a copper more, I promise.
Ledger update: salt in {town} at {gold} a sack. The river guild will hate that, and I do not mind a bit.

encounter_trade_offer.text: Ser {player}, I will give you {gold} for that load of wool at {town}. Fair price, and you keep your dignity.
Ser {player}, you look like a shrewd sort. Shall we haggle? {gold} for the lot, and no hard feelings after.
Ser {player}, {gold} for the wool and I am on my way to {town}. That is a generous offer, I assure you.
Ser {player}, a deal is a deal, and {gold} is what the salt market will bear this season. Take it or leave it.
Ser {player}, I still remember the ambush, yet a fair deal is a fair deal. I offer {gold}, and I want nothing else from you.

encounter_greeting.text: Ser {player}, {persona} of {my_faction} here. Good to see a familiar face on this cursed road. Shall we trade?
Ser {player}, {persona} of {my_faction}. I have salt in these wagons and no quarrel with you. Let us keep it that way, shall we?
Ser {player}, {persona} of {my_faction}. Stand aside with your men, or let us talk terms like merchants and not brawlers.
Ser {player}, {persona} from {my_faction}. Our carts are full, our purses are open, and I would rather not spill blood over a bad price.

player_raided_my_village.text: Fire in {village} costs a fortune in salt and wool. Ser {player}, I expect a settlement, or I expect the guild to hear of it.
Ser {player}, you burned {village} and now every wagon detours around it. Is that what you wanted for your ledger?
Burning {village} was a poor return on investment, Ser {player}. The carts will simply stop coming, and that hurts everyone.
Ser {player}, I can forgive a lot for a good deal. Burning {village} is not a deal, so let us talk reparations.

war_declared.text: War with {enemy_faction} is terrible for wool prices. {my_faction} will pay for this in tolls and lost caravans.
{my_faction} has declared war on {enemy_faction}. Every road is closed and my salt is rotting in the cart.
So {my_faction} and {enemy_faction} are at war. Lovely. My caravans will now pay a toll at every gate.
Bandits love a war, and {enemy_faction} smells of gold. Let us hope someone thinks of the merchants first.

peace_made.text: Peace between {my_faction} and {faction} at last. The roads reopen and the salt carts can finally earn their keep.
{my_faction} and {faction} have signed terms. I will drink to that, and then I will count the profits.
Peace with {faction}, is it? Tolls may fall for a season, and I plan to make the most of it.
Good news for every caravan on the road: {my_faction} is at peace with {faction}. Get your wagons moving.

released_by_player.text: Ser {player} let me go without ransom. That is a rare kindness, and I will remember it in my ledger.
Ser {player}, you released me without a ransom. I will not forget that, and my next deal is on me.
Ser {player} freed me from captivity rather than ransom. An odd choice, but I have no complaint with it.
Ser {player}, releasing me for nothing is a strange move. Next time a ransom would be more useful to both of us.

beat_by_player.text: Ser {player} beat us with {troop_count} men at the ford. The cost of wagons and wages is brutal, I tell you.
Ser {player}, your {troop_count} men caught us on the crossing. A fair fight, but my wagons paid the price.
Ser {player}, {troop_count} of your men and a clever flank. I lost the field, but I will buy you a drink in town.
Ser {player}, {troop_count} men and a lucky wind. I will have my silver back one day, mark my words.
Ser {player} won the field against us with {troop_count} troops. Honest work, and I respect a clean victory.

whisper_beg_help.text: Ser {player}, {fief} will fall unless someone rides to help. I will pay in salt and silver if you come quickly.
Ser {player}, {fief} is under siege by {enemy_faction} and my cargo is trapped inside. Help me, and I will pay well.
Ser {player}, {enemy_faction} is at the gates of {fief}. My wagons and silver are at risk. Can you spare some men?
My friend, {enemy_faction} has the road to {fief} blocked and my cargo is trapped inside. Could you lend a hand?

ambient_complaint.text: Bandits on the {town} road took another wagon today. Terrible for trade, and the road tolls still come due.
{faction} has doubled the bridge toll again. Nobody asks the merchants who keep their coffers full, hm?
{rival} is undercutting every salt seller from here to Imzellan. Dumping stock below cost is not a business plan.
Tolls on the {town} crossing climbed again. I have found a dry ford, and I will not be telling anyone where.

ambient_chatter.text: Rain over {town} again, so the wool bales will be soggy by the time they reach the market.
Anyone on the {village} road seen a decent caravan of salt? I would sell my own mule for a dry road today.
Lag on the server is eating my bargaining time. Please hurry up and let me sell in peace.
Finest bread in {village} this morning, and I bought two loaves for the road. Worth every copper.
The map shows a bridge near {town}. If it holds, that is a shorter route and a fatter margin.
